Heads of development (or capital) expenditure (Heads of Developmental Expenditures)

By it is meant such expenditure as becomes the cause of increase in the economic development of the country, e.g. making railways, roads and canals, constructing projects of irrigation and hydro-electricity, giving practical shape to plans of post, telegraph and telephone, and spending money on schemes of agricultural and industrial development. The annual development expenditure of the Government of Pakistan is on the following heads:

the development programme of corporations, the regular development programme of provinces, water, energy, agriculture, industry, transport, communications, physical planning and housing, education and training, public health, population planning, social action programme etc. During 2009-10 a total of 518 billion rupees were spent on development purposes, which were 18.5 per cent of total expenditure and 4 per cent of gross domestic product.

Development expenditure is made in the government sector for the growth and development of the national economy. In other words, this is equal to fixed capital formation (Capital Formation) in the government sector. Its volume depends on those development projects which are included in the annual development programme (ADP). In it capital expenditure occurring on both “physical and social infrastructure” (Infrastructure) is included. During the non-planned period (1970-71 to 1977-78) (since the government was much more a partner in the economic and business activities of the country, therefore) in the “annual development plan” an increase kept occurring at an annual rate of 35 per cent, because of which the share of the government sector in total investment increased from 48 per cent in 1971-72 to 66 per cent in 1977-78. But later, when the era of the development and encouragement of the private sector, i.e. privatisation (Privatization), began, the annual rate of increase in the annual development plan (ADP) decreased, and the share of the government sector in the total investment of the country too decreased.

Generally, for the completion of the annual development programme, seventy per cent is spent through the federal government and thirty per cent through the provincial governments. The most money is spent on the development of water resources. After it on transport and communications.

With regard to the expenditure of different sectors the relative importance is this: water, energy, communications and transport, rural development, population welfare, physical planning, education and training, health, agriculture and industry.

Capital or development budget (Capital Budget)

It has been told behind that the budget of the government is of two kinds: the revenue budget and the capital budget. We have done a detailed discussion on the former behind; therefore now we explain the capital budget. It is also called the annual development programme (Annual Development Programme: ADP). It consists of two parts. On one side there are capital collections, i.e. resources, as it were, the amount which the government obtains from different sources, and on the other side capital payments. Resources are of two kinds: internal and external. There are two sources of internal resources: first, the federal fund; second, loans. External resources consist of different kinds of aid, e.g. project loans, commodity loans, and non-project aid etc.

There are two parts of capital expenditure: development and non-development expenditure. Development expenditure is made in three ways: expenditure in the government sector, development aid of provinces, and expenditure in the private sector. There are several further heads of the government sector. By non-development expenditure are meant the amounts which are spent on maintaining development projects.

paras.pashto: ۱. له هېوادنیو سرچینو بشپړه ګټه واخیستل شي او د اقتصادي پرمختګ په چټکولو د خلکو د ژوند معیار ښه شي.

paras.text: 2. To stop inflation government expenditure should be reduced and surplus money should not be issued, so that the trend of prices can be downward.
paras.urdu: 2۔ افراطِ زر کو روکنے کے لئے سرکاری اخراجات کم کئے جائیں اور زائد زر جاری نہ کیا جائے تاکہ قیمتوں کا رجحان نیچے کی طرف ہو سکے۔
paras.pashto: ۲. د انفلاسیون د مخنیوي لپاره دولتي لګښتونه کم شي او اضافي پیسې جاري نشي، تر څو د بیو تمایل ښکته شي.

paras.text: 3. As much foreign exchange as possible should be earned, so that goods of daily use, and raw material and machines etc. for new industries can be imported.
paras.urdu: 3۔ زیادہ سے زیادہ زرِ مبادلہ کمایا جائے، تاکہ روزمرہ کے استعمال کی اشیاء اور نئی نئی صنعتوں کے لئے خام مال اور مشینیں وغیرہ درآمد کی جا سکیں۔
paras.pashto: ۳. تر ډېره ډېر بهرني اسعار وګټل شي، تر څو د ورځنۍ کارونې توکي او د نویو صنعتونو لپاره خام مواد او ماشینونه او نور وارد شي.

paras.text: 4. Such conditions should be created in the country that encouragement is given to putting as much capital as possible in business here, the production of things increases and prices become less.

paras.pashto: ۴. په هېواد کې داسې حالات رامنځته شي چې دلته په کاروبار کې د ډېرې ډېرې پانګې د لګولو هڅونه وشي، د شیانو تولید زیات شي او بیې کمې شي.

paras.text: 5. People should be encouraged to save money, so that for development purposes financial resources can be available from within the country itself, and dependence on foreign aid (Foreign Aid) becomes less.

paras.text: 6. The economic imbalance which is found in different parts and areas of the country should be removed.

(continued from p.234) … economy is deeply affected, therefore the government, while making its fiscal policy, keeps the following purposes in front:

1. Full benefit should be taken from national resources and, by speeding up economic development, the standard of living of people should be made better.

2. To stop inflation government expenditure should be reduced and surplus money should not be issued, so that the trend of prices can be downward.

3. As much foreign exchange as possible should be earned, so that goods of daily use, and raw material and machines etc. for new industries can be imported.

4. Such conditions should be created in the country that encouragement is given to putting as much capital as possible in business here, the production of things increases and prices become less.

5. People should be encouraged to save money, so that for development purposes financial resources can be available from within the country itself, and dependence on foreign aid (Foreign Aid) becomes less.

6. The economic imbalance which is found in different parts and areas of the country should be removed.

7. Private business should be encouraged; however, monopolies should be discouraged.

8. Most of the national wealth should not come to be collected in the hands of a few individuals.

9. Effort should be made to create a strong middle class in the country.

10. Giving all-round development to social sectors so that the nation can become prosperous.

11. Increasing agricultural and industrial production as much as possible so that, making Pakistan self-sufficient, freedom can be obtained from dependence on foreign countries.

12. To make “self-employment schemes” (Self-Employment Schemes) successful for the common man, providing as many financial resources as possible and increasing the opportunities of employment.

(continued from p.234) … economy is deeply affected, therefore the government, while making its fiscal policy, keeps the following purposes in front:

1. Full benefit should be taken from national resources and, by speeding up economic development, the standard of living of people should be made better.

2. To stop inflation government expenditure should be reduced and surplus money should not be issued, so that the trend of prices can be downward.

3. As much foreign exchange as possible should be earned, so that goods of daily use, and raw material and machines etc. for new industries can be imported.

4. Such conditions should be created in the country that encouragement is given to putting as much capital as possible in business here, the production of things increases and prices become less.

5. People should be encouraged to save money, so that for development purposes financial resources can be available from within the country itself, and dependence on foreign aid (Foreign Aid) becomes less.

6. The economic imbalance which is found in different parts and areas of the country should be removed.

7. Private business should be encouraged; however, monopolies should be discouraged.

8. Most of the national wealth should not come to be collected in the hands of a few individuals.

9. Effort should be made to create a strong middle class in the country.

10. Giving all-round development to social sectors so that the nation can become prosperous.

11. Increasing agricultural and industrial production as much as possible so that, making Pakistan self-sufficient, freedom can be obtained from dependence on foreign countries.

12. To make “self-employment schemes” (Self-Employment Schemes) successful for the common man, providing as many financial resources as possible and increasing the opportunities of employment.

13. Obtaining resources from the wealthy class and transferring them towards the poor class, so that the distribution of economic prosperity can be on equal and just foundations.

14. Establishing a system of justice and benevolence, so that progress, prosperity and national stability can be created in the country.

Sources of revenue of provincial governments in Pakistan (Sources of Revenue of Provincial Governments)

Pakistan has four provincial governments: the Government of Punjab, the Government of Sindh, the Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the Government of Balochistan, which in their sphere of work perform political, administrative, economic and social functions, and for their payment obtain income from different sources. 9۔ ملک میں مضبوط، متوسط طبقہ پیدا کرنے کی کوشش کی جائے۔

10۔ معاشرتی شعبوں کو ہمہ پہلو ترقی دینا تاکہ قوم خوشحال ہو سکے۔

11۔ زرعی اور صنعتی پیداوار میں زیادہ سے زیادہ اضافہ کرنا تاکہ پاکستان کو خود کفیل بنا کر غیر ملکی محتاجی سے چھٹکارا حاصل کیا جائے۔

12۔ عام آدمی کے لئے ”خود روزگاری سکیموں“ (Self-Employment Schemes) کو کامیاب بنانے کے لئے زیادہ سے زیادہ مالی وسائل فراہم کر کے روزگار کے مواقع میں اضافہ کرنا۔

13۔ دولت مند طبقہ سے وسائل حاصل کر کے غریب طبقہ کی طرف منتقل کرنا، تاکہ معاشی خوشحالی کی تقسیم مساویانہ اور عادلانہ بنیادوں پر ہو سکے۔

14۔ عدل و احسان کا نظام قائم کرنا تاکہ ملک میں ترقی، خوشحالی اور قومی استحکام پیدا کیا جا سکے۔

پاکستان میں صوبائی حکومتوں کے ذرائعِ آمدنی (Sources of Revenue of Provincial Governments)

پاکستان کی چار صوبائی حکومتیں ہیں: حکومت پنجاب، حکومت سندھ، حکومت خیبر پختونخواہ اور حکومت بلوچستان جو اپنے دائرہ کار میں، سیاسی، انتظامی، اقتصادی اور معاشرتی فرائض انجام دیتی ہیں اور ان کی ادائیگی کے لئے مختلف ذرائع سے آمدنی حاصل کرتی ہیں۔ صوبائی حکومتوں کے بھی دو طرح کے بجٹ ہوتے ہیں: اول، ریونیو یا محاصلاتی بجٹ اور دوم، سرمایاتی بجٹ۔ محاصلاتی بجٹ کے مندرجہ ذیل ذرائع ہیں:

صوبائی حکومتوں کی آمدنی کا سب سے بڑا ذریعہ وفاقی حکومت کے نافذ کردہ ٹیکسوں سے ملنے والا حصہ ہے۔ دوسرے نمبر پر صوبائی حکومتوں کے نافذ کردہ ٹیکسوں سے حاصل ہونے والی رقم ہے۔ اہم ذرائعِ آمدنی کی وضاحت ذیل میں کی گئی ہے:

1۔ مرکزی حکومت کے ٹیکسوں کا حصہ (Share of Federal Government Taxes):
